Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test exercises IteratorUtils.collatedIterator with a null comparator in two ways:

- It verifies that passing a null iterator triggers a NullPointerException. This is enforced by CollatingIterator.addIterator, which checks for null and throws NPE. That part behaves as expected.

- It then builds a collated iterator with a null comparator and two valid iterators, expecting “natural ordering” to be used (per the Javadoc) when the comparator is null.

The implementation path is:

- IteratorUtils.collatedIterator(null, iterator1, iterator2) simply constructs a new CollatingIterator with the provided comparator and iterators:
  - org.apache.commons.collections4.IteratorUtils.collatedIterator(...):
    return new CollatingIterator<E>(comparator, iterator1, iterator2);

- CollatingIterator stores the comparator as-is via setComparator without applying any default:
  - CollatingIterator(comp, a, b) → this(comp, 2); addIterator(a); addIterator(b);
  - CollatingIterator(comp, int) → setComparator(comp);
  - setComparator(comp) → comparator = comp; (no substitution for null)

- When the iterator is used, next() calls least() to find the smallest current element among the underlying iterators. least() compares elements using the stored comparator. Because setComparator accepted a null comparator and did not substitute natural ordering, the first comparison attempt will dereference a null comparator, causing a NullPointerException on first use.

This directly matches the bug report: with a null comparator, natural ordering should be used, but the code leaves the comparator null, leading to an exception the first time the returned iterator is used.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
